title: infrastructure-weekly-update-2026-06-15
content:
Weekly update (week ending 2026-06-15) - Infrastructure team

Owner: Ethan Reynolds; collaborators: Priya Desai, Carlos Mendez, Li Wei, Maya Thompson

Highlights
- GPU pool steady but stressed in US/EMEA peak windows. Average cluster utilization across all regions this week: 62% (down slightly from 65% last week).
- Small incident in us-west-2 on 2026-06-12 caused ~45 minutes of degraded capacity for dedicated pools; mitigation path validated.
- Autoscaling burst policy rollout for Dedicated pools completed in staging and initial canary in prod (5% traffic). Cold-start median down to 320ms; 95th percentile ~1.8s.
- Cost optimization experiment (bfloat16 path for select models) shows ~18% reduced token compute cost for encoder-heavy workloads.

Fleet metrics (2026-06-08 -> 2026-06-15)
- Total GPUs in fleet: 1,200 (across us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, eu-west-2, ap-northeast-1)
- Avg utilization: 62%
- Peak utilization (24h window): 89% in us-east-1 on 2026-06-13 (evening PT)
- Average queue depth (workload backlog): 15% of cluster capacity during peak windows
- Instance health: node-level NPU/drivers OK after rolling update; 7 nodes replaced this week due to thermal sensor faults

Incidents
- INFRA-419 (us-west-2 degraded capacity) - Summary: a RAID controller on a hypernode failed under heavy GC activity, causing IO contention and eviction of several inference workers. Impact: 45 minutes of elevated error rates for Dedicated pools in us-west-2; affected customers automatically failed over to compatible model variants in us-east-1.
  - Root cause: intermittent RAID controller firmware regression exposed by increased checkpointing concurrency.
  - Mitigation: rollback firmware to vetted rev + throttle checkpoint concurrency in runtime (hotfix deployed 2026-06-13).
  - Postmortem planned; owner: Priya Desai; ETA doc: 2026-06-18.

Capacity planning and procurement
- Q3 projection: expected workload growth ~30% driven by two mid-market customers moving to Dedicated and increased embedding throughput from analytics workloads.
- Short-term (next 6 weeks): aim to add 200 H100-ish GPUs (preferred) across us-east-1 and eu-west-2 to cover forecasted peak. Current procurement update: vendor notified of 2-week delay on partial shipment (new ETA 2026-07-20). Procurement lead: Carlos Mendez.
- Contingency: enable additional burst capacity across partner cloud accounts (contracted spare capacity) to cover immediate shortfall during peak windows. Legal already approved burn-rate clause for short-term rentals.

Regions / Deployments
- eu-west-2 expansion: control plane and private deployment images validated; first Private customer onboarding scheduled for 2026-06-22. Initial benchmarks show 10% higher tail latency than eu-west-1 for long-context workloads; investigating network MTU and VF configuration.
- ap-northeast-1: stable; no capacity alarms.

Performance tuning / cost work
- Bfloat16 code path: completed validation on top-10 models; 18% average compute cost reduction for applicable models with negligible quality regression on internal evals. Rollout plan: phase 1 enablement for non-latency-sensitive Dedicated routes week of 2026-06-29.
- KV cache warmup improvement pushed to staging - reduced prefix re-encode token load by ~22%.

Operational changes / runbook updates
- Added RAID controller health entries to the GPU fleet runbook and expanded the node-replacement playbook. Confluence doc updated.
- Short outage mitigation template updated to include automatic routing to warm spare regions and immediate communication steps for CS/AE teams.

Standup notes / meeting log (selected)
- Mon 2026-06-08: tracked two thermal-fault nodes; scheduled replacements Tue morning.
- Wed 2026-06-10: validated autoscaler burst policy in staging; flagged cold-start latency outliers.
- Thu 2026-06-11: runbook dry run for regional failovers - success in simulated traffic shift.
- Fri 2026-06-12: INFRA-419 surfaced during evening peak; mitigation enacted, customers failed over.

Action items / owners
- Priya: postmortem for INFRA-419 + recommend firmware gating policy (ETA 2026-06-18).
- Carlos: finalize purchase order and confirm revised H100 partial shipment ETA; identify temporary spot capacity sources (ETA 2026-06-19).
- Li: continue KV cache warmup rollout to canary routing (ETA 2026-06-22).
- Maya: run eu-west-2 network MTU and VF tuning experiments; report latency delta breakdown (ETA 2026-06-19).
- Ethan: coordinate communication plan with CS/AE for customers likely to hit dedicated capacity constraints in July (ETA 2026-06-17).

Risks / Blockers
- Procurement delay for H100s creates exposure if Q3 growth accelerates beyond forecast; contingency is short-term partner bursts but at higher cost.
- One remaining firmware revision candidate for RAID firmware needs vendor signoff before fleet-wide rollout.

Next week priorities (2026-06-16 -> 2026-06-22)
1) Ship INFRA-419 postmortem and firmware gating checklist.
2) Confirm temporary capacity plan and execute partner burst contracts if needed.
3) Continue canary rollouts for bfloat16 and KV cache warmup.
4) Finish eu-west-2 tuning and onboard first Private customer.
5) Improve autoscaler observability to capture 95/99th cold-start causes.

Notes / misc
- CS flagged two customers who may cross our Dedicated uplift threshold in early July - outreach planned after procurement confirmation.
- We should prep a short comms template for customers describing temporary spillover behavior and expected mitigations.

If you have questions or need deeper metrics slices (per-model, per-pool), ping me or open INFRA-427.
